CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up of chronic arthritis, gout, and reflux.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Anna is a 44-year-old female presenting for follow-up of chronic medical problems. She reports significant improvement in her arthritis, particularly in her right knee, after completing physical therapy and engaging in regular exercise including pilates and weight lifting. She is now able to walk 1-1.5 miles daily. Regarding her gout, she had an episode of right first toe gout approximately two months ago that resolved with medication. She is compliant with allopurinol and denies further flare-ups. For her reflux, she reports partial dietary modifications but continues to experience morning vomiting and some episodes of reflux. She also endorses abdominal pain and bloating. She denies diarrhea, weight loss, fever, or chills. Last bowel movement was two days ago and was normal without blood.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and abdominal distension. Negative for diarrhea, fever, chills, weight loss, and hematochezia.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Arthritis, gout, gastroesophageal reflux disease.

MEDICATIONS
Omeprazole 40 mg once daily, allopurinol 100 mg once daily.

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient engages in regular exercise including pilates and weight lifting.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: unremarkable. Cardiovascular: heart sounds normal. Pulmonary: lungs clear to auscultation bilaterally. Abdomen: tenderness to right upper quadrant on palpation, no rebound or guarding, no peritoneal signs. Right knee: mild effusion, slight pain to palpation, decreased range of motion.

RESULTS
Autoimmune panel: normal. Right knee x-ray: no fracture, residual arthritis present.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Reflux/nausea/vomiting: Continue omeprazole 40 mg once daily. Continue dietary modifications. Order right upper quadrant ultrasound to rule out gallstones. Check labs.
2. Gout: Well-controlled. Continue allopurinol 100 mg once daily. Refill prescribed.
3. Arthritis: Significant improvement noted. Continue current exercise regimen with pilates and weight bearing. Follow-up as needed for further imaging or intervention.
